title: Ayurveda at the Crossroads of Tradition, Evidence and Global Health
subtitle: Growing Ayush economy, rising domestic adoption, medical value travel and research are opening new avenues for Ayurveda’s global expansion
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 5:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Ayurveda is moving from the margins of global health conversations towards the mainstream. India’s expanding Ayush economy, growing domestic use of traditional systems and rising interest in wellness and medical value travel are creating new opportunities for Ayurveda, even as the global health community places greater emphasis on traditional medicine, research and evidence.
As India marks the 11th Ayurveda Day on September 23, 2026, the moment is significant. The theme, “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow”, comes at a time when India is seeking to connect its centuries-old knowledge system with modern research, quality standards and international healthcare frameworks. The challenge now is not simply to take Ayurveda to the world, but to build the evidence, credibility and institutional foundations that can support its responsible global growth.
Over the past decade, the Ayush sector has witnessed significant economic expansion, creating a stronger foundation for the growth and wider adoption of Ayurveda. The Ayush market grew from USD 2.85 billion in 2014 to USD 43.4 billion in 2023, while Ayush exports increased from USD 1.09 billion to USD 2.16 billion during the same period. Government initiatives have also focused on strengthening MSMEs and startups, helping create a broader ecosystem for entrepreneurship, innovation and investment in the sector.
The growing domestic acceptance of Ayush systems provides another important foundation for this expansion. The first exclusive All-India Survey on Ayush, conducted by the National Sample Survey Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation during July 2022–June 2023, covered 1,81,298 households, including 1,04,195 rural and 77,103 urban households. The survey recorded Ayush awareness levels of 94.8 per cent in rural areas and 96 per cent in urban areas. It also found that 46.3 per cent of rural residents and 52.9 per cent of urban residents had used Ayush for treatment or prevention during the preceding 365 days. Ayurveda emerged as the most commonly used Ayush system for treatment, indicating its substantial domestic base and potential contribution to preventive healthcare and wellness.
India is also seeking to leverage the growing global demand for holistic healthcare through medical value travel. A dedicated Ayush Visa was introduced on July 27, 2023, for foreign nationals seeking treatment under Ayush systems. The Government has also partnered with the India Tourism Development Corporation to identify tourism circuits with potential for Ayurveda and other traditional systems. The global medical value travel market, estimated at USD 115.6 billion in 2022, is projected to reach approximately USD 286.1 billion by 2030. Ayurveda and other traditional systems can therefore become an important component of India’s medical value travel and wellness ecosystem by bringing together healthcare services, wellness offerings and tourism.
A significant policy development in this direction has been the release of NITI Aayog’s “Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global” in July 2026. Envisioned as a long-term pathway up to 2047, the roadmap focuses on regulation and standards, research, education, international collaboration, exports, branding and medical value travel. It emphasises the need for quality standards, robust infrastructure, credible research, trained professionals, consistent products and regulatory frameworks that can be understood and recognised internationally. The roadmap seeks to create the institutional and quality ecosystem necessary for Ayurveda’s responsible expansion and greater confidence in its services and products in international markets.
India’s efforts to strengthen Ayurveda are also closely linked with its wider engagement in global traditional, complementary and integrative medicine. The WHO Global Traditional Medicine Strategy 2025–2034, adopted by the 78th World Health Assembly in 2025, provides a global framework for strengthening evidence, ensuring safety and regulation, integrating traditional medicine into health systems and optimising its wider cross-sectoral contribution.
India has played a significant role in this global movement. The WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat, was established in 2022 with India as its lead investor. India committed an estimated USD 250 million towards its establishment, infrastructure and operations. The Centre focuses on evidence and learning, data and analytics, sustainability and equity, and innovation and technology.
India’s role was further reflected in the two WHO Global Summits on Traditional Medicine. The first, held in Gandhinagar in August 2023 and co-hosted by WHO and the Government of India, resulted in the Gujarat Declaration. The second summit, held in New Delhi from December 17–19, 2025, under the theme “Restoring Balance for People and Planet: The Science and Practice of Well-being”, addressed issues including evidence, health-system integration, regulation, biodiversity, indigenous knowledge, intellectual property and innovation. The summit resulted in the Delhi Declaration and SMART—Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound—commitments towards implementation of the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Strategy 2025–2034.
Another important development has been the inclusion of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani in global health classification frameworks. In January 2024, WHO launched Traditional Medicine Module 2 of ICD-11, covering morbidity codes for these systems and enabling their conditions to be documented and reported through an internationally comparable framework. WHO has clarified that such inclusion does not constitute an endorsement of the scientific validity or efficacy of individual traditional medicine practices. Work is also progressing towards the classification of interventions, with India and WHO working on intervention codes for Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani.
At the heart of Ayurveda’s future development is the generation of credible scientific evidence. The Ministry of Ayush’s Ayush Research Portal serves as a Government repository of research on Ayush systems and currently displays more than 43,000 research entries. This growing body of research can contribute to greater scientific understanding of Ayurveda and support the development of credible standards, services and products. At the same time, preserving the distinctive principles and knowledge systems of Ayurveda remains essential to ensuring its responsible and sustainable development.
The emerging picture is therefore one of an Indian traditional health system moving into a new phase of global engagement. A rapidly expanding Ayush economy, growing domestic adoption, new opportunities in medical value travel, stronger international cooperation, global classification frameworks and increasing emphasis on research and quality standards are collectively creating new avenues for Ayurveda.
As the country marks the 11th Ayurveda Day, the focus on “Ayurveda for a Healthier Tomorrow” provides an opportunity to highlight the system’s potential contribution to preventive healthcare, wellbeing and sustainable living. At the same time, its future global journey will increasingly depend on evidence, innovation, quality, professional capacity and responsible globalisation—strengthening Ayurveda’s place in the evolving landscape of health and wellness.

title: Commercial Coal Mine Auctions: Powering Aatmanirbhar Bharat Through Transparency
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 11:19AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Coal block allocation in India has undergone a significant transformation over the past decade. Following the Supreme Court's cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014, allocation moved to a transparent, rules-based process. The launch of commercial coal mine auctions by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 18 June 2020 marked the next major step. Six years on, it has become one of the most consequential structural reforms in the mining sector, delivering benefits shared transparently across industry, the exchequer and coal-bearing communities.
The entire process has been kept transparent. Bidding is conducted online in two stages on the MSTC platform, with bid documents decrypted and opened live in front of bidders. There is no end-use restriction, 100% FDI is allowed through the automatic route, and upfront payments are kept low and adjustable against future revenue share, keeping the field open to smaller and newer players. The Policy has been such a success that 147 coal mines have been auctioned till date with 44 new companies winning a coal mine. The Policy has not only attracted private players but also legacy coal PSUs like Coal India's own subsidiaries — Western Coalfields Limited (WCL) and Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL), traditionally only producers and sellers of coal — have themselves stepped in as bidders for blocks in recent rounds, competing on exactly the same terms as private players.
Every auctioned block contributes a strong share to the states in the form of revenue share (the competitively bid revenue share, additional to royalty), Royalty (statutory, to the state), DMF contributions (ploughed back into the mining district via PMKKKY), NMET contributions (funding future exploration) and GST. Since 2020, 147 coal blocks have been auctioned across nine states, projected to generate approx.₹47,500 crore in annual revenue, ₹55,000 crore in capital investment and 4.9 lakh jobs. In the Financial Year 2025-26, the total revenue generated (from upfront & premium payment) from allocated commercial mines was about Rs. 3090 Cr.
The revenue story runs alongside a production story. Coal output from only commercial mines grew from 12.55 million tonnes in FY 2023-24 to 23.51 million tonnes in FY 2024-25. Captive and commercial blocks together produced about 210 MT in FY 2025-26, crossing the 200 million tonne mark for the first time. A decade earlier the figure stood at 28.8 MT, hence showcasing a compound annual growth of about 22 per cent over the period. Every additional tonne mined domestically is a tonne that need not be imported, directly supporting India's push toward self-reliance in coal.
Transparent, technology-enabled bidding that keeps attracting new entrants; a level playing field open enough that even government miners now compete for blocks rather than being handed them; and a revenue-sharing design — royalty, premium, DMF and NMET stacked together — that has nearly tripled states' coal revenue in a decade: together, these make the commercial coal mine auction regime a genuine win-win for states, industry, local communities and the nation's energy security alike.

title: India and MERCOSUR Sign First Additional Protocol to Facilitate Electronic Certificates of Origin
subtitle: Protocol to Facilitate Paperless Trade and Modernise Customs Procedures under India–MERCOSUR Preferential Trade Agreement
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 4:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India and MERCOSUR signed the First Additional Protocol to the India–MERCOSUR Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) to facilitate acceptance of electronic Certificates of Origin, marking an important step towards facilitating paperless trade and modernising customs procedures between India and the MERCOSUR countries.
The Protocol was signed by Commerce Secretary, Government of India, Shri Rajesh Agarwal and Ambassador of Uruguay to India H.E. Mr Alberto Guani, and Ambassador of Paraguay to India, H.E. Mr Fleming Raul Duarte Ramos, in the presence of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay H.E. Mr Mario Lubetkin, in the exercise of the Pro Tempore Presidency of MERCOSUR and the representatives from Embassies of Argentina & Brazil.
The India-MERCOSUR PTA was signed on 25 January 2004 and entered into force on 1 June 2009. The Agreement provides preferential tariff concessions on 450 tariff lines by India and 452 tariff lines by the MERCOSUR side.
The First Additional Protocol amends Article 16 of Annex III (Rules of Origin) of the PTA by providing that Certificates of Origin issued in electronic format shall have the same legal validity and identical value as Certificates of Origin issued in paper format. Such electronic Certificates of Origin will be required to be issued and electronically signed in accordance with the respective domestic legislation of the Parties, by duly authorised entities and officials.
The move is expected to facilitate the transition towards digital and paperless trade documentation, reduce transaction costs and processing time associated with the issuance and verification of Certificates of Origin, and improve the efficiency of preferential trade under the existing India-MERCOSUR PTA.
The initiative follows discussions in the Joint Administrative Committee of the India-MERCOSUR PTA. At its fourth meeting held on 27 November 2025, both sides supported updating the Agreement to facilitate the use of digital Certificates of Origin. The proposal for the Additional Protocol was subsequently adopted by mutual consent at the fifth meeting of the Joint Administrative Committee held on 9 April 2026.
The Protocol will enter into force upon completion of the respective internal procedures by India and the MERCOSUR Parties and notification of the same to each other.
The signing of the First Additional Protocol underscores the commitment of India and MERCOSUR to deepen trade facilitation, adopt modern customs practices and strengthen the institutional framework supporting bilateral trade.
The signing also represents a significant step in the ongoing engagement between India and MERCOSUR to further strengthen and expand their trade and economic partnership.

title: INDIAN AIR FORCE DRONATHON - 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Vice Chief of the Air Staff, inaugurated the first Indian Air Force Dronathon-2026 at the Pokhran Field Firing Range, Jaisalmer, today. The inaugural ceremony was attended by senior functionaries of MoD, HQ IDS and representatives from Indian Army, and BSF. Dronathon-2026 is an IAF initiative aimed at engaging directly with the Indian unmanned systems industry and assessing emerging technologies under realistic operational conditions. The three-day event, planned from 14 to 16 September 2026, brings together over 20 leading defence companies, start-ups MSMEs, DPSUs and innovators from India's rapidly evolving unmanned systems ecosystem.
The IAF views unmanned systems as an important complement to manned aviation providing commanders with additional options to enhance the reach, persistence responsiveness and flexibility of air operations During the Dronathon, participating companies and innovators will demonstrate their Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) and associated technologies at the Pokhran range.
The demonstrations will encompass a wide spectrum of operational capabilities including surveillance and reconnaissance, autonomous operations, swarm technologies, electronic warfare and Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems (CUAS). The central focus of Dronathon-2026 is to move from technology demonstration to operational effect. The systems are being assessed for their reliability, and effectiveness in demanding and contested environments, as well as their ability to adapt to evolving operational requirements and emerging threats.
During the event today, the VCAS also released the ‘IAF UAS Roadmap’, providing greater clarity to Indian industry on capability priorities. The roadmap is intended to facilitate focused innovation and enable the unmanned airborne systems industry, academia and research organisations to align their efforts with the future requirements of the IAF.
On the opening day of Dronathon-2026, the Indian Air Force successfully demonstrated a key capability of "Vayu UTtaM," its indigenously developed multi-mode Unmanned Traffic Management (UTM) system. During its real time demonstration at Pokhran, it detected and tracked both military and civil UAS. The capability is designed to facilitate coordinated management of UAS operations in increasingly congested airspace, while also supporting the identification and timely mitigation of unauthorised or rogue drones. With the increasing proliferation of UAS, Vayu UTtaM has potential applications beyond the military domain, including in areas related to airspace safety, critical infrastructure, civil aviation and public safety.
Dronathon-2026 reinforces the IAF's commitment to Atmanirbharta in unmanned systems, with the focus extending beyond airframes to the complete ecosystem, including propulsion, sensors and payloads, communications, autonomy, electronic warfare, countermeasures and airspace management.

Apart from playing an indispensable role in maintaining a healthy ecosystem, GIB serves as a unique cultural symbol of India's arid heritage.

To ensure GIB is protected, India is laying great emphasis on its conservation.

Towards that end, today inaugurated the Soft Release Centre for GIB in the facility. The Soft Release Centre is equipped with infrastructure designed to support the conservation, monitoring and gradual adaptation of GIBs to the natural environment.
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
September 14, 2026

Shri Yadav
inaugurated the Soft Release Centre for the Great Indian Bustard at the facility, and interacted with officials of the Wildlife Institute of India, the Gujarat Forest Department and other stakeholders engaged in the species' conservation. . It

ed
restoration of around 11 sq. km. of grassland infested with the invasive Prosopis juliflora

aising of 30 km. of predator-proof fencing covering 15 sq. km.
; The
pioneering 'jump-start' intervention in which infertile eggs laid by wild GIB females were replaced with viable eggs from the conservation breeding programme.
Shri Yadav
was informed that the resulting chick from the second such attempt has survived beyond the critical first three months in the wild – a landmark result for the species' recovery in Gujarat.
During my visit to the Great Indian Bustard Habitat in Naliya, Kutch, interacted with representatives of the Jat Sumra and Darbar communities in 'Khatala Sabha' to garner their support in the conservation efforts of the Great Indian Bustard.

Under the leadership of PM Shri @narendramodi ji, India has been laying emphasis on community-led stewardship for environmental protection and species conservation. The local pastoralist and agricultural groups in Kutch are key to ensuring the success of GIB conservation. 

Later, flagged off 33 new patrolling and rescue vehicles for forest and wildlife conservation efforts which will be used in various divisions under the Kutch Forest Circle for forest protection, forest development, wildlife protection, field patrolling, monitoring, and quick response activities.
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
September 14, 2026
Shri Yadav
appreciated the coordinated efforts of the Gujarat Forest Department and the Wildlife Institute of India in advancing this achievement.

ach
chh Forest Circle for forest protection, forest development, wildlife protection, field patrolling, monitoring and quick-response activities.
The Minister subsequently visited the Hariyalu Gram plantation in Sayara and was briefed on the Sayara Van Kavach initiative and an associated bee-keeping unit. He undertook tree plantation at the site, inaugurated the Sayara Van Kavach, and witnessed the exchange of a Memorandum of Understanding with the Deendayal Port Authority for plantation activities. The Minister also released the Van Kavach Photobook and interacted with local residents, distributing plant saplings among them.
Inaugurated the Van Kavach at Modpir Dada Temple in Sanyara, Kutch today and planted a bargad sapling along with Shri @arjunmodhwadia and other public representatives. 

I commend Gujarat for adopting the 'Van Kavach' model to develop dense, green, and biodiversity-rich forest areas within limited spaces in both urban and rural areas. 

‘Van Kavach' is not merely tree plantation; it is a natural green protective shield developed around human settlements. 

It brings together tree plantation, biodiversity conservation, carbon sequestration, environmental education, and public participation.
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
September 14, 2026
The Sayara Van Kavach, developed over 9.46 sq. km. site following the Miyawaki method of dense, multi-layered afforestation, comprises over 10,000 saplings across 47 native species suited to the saline, low-water conditions of Kachchh. Shri Yadav was informed that the model is expected to lower local temperatures by 1.5–2°C, aid groundwater recharge, prevent soil erosion, and provide a natural habitat for birds, insects and small wildlife, besides serving as a site for eco-tourism, environmental education and local employment.
At Jakhau,
the Minister
visited the Mangrove Nursery and undertook mangrove plantation alongside about 50 personnel of the Border Security Force and over 50 local residents at an adjoining site. He viewed a photo exhibition on mangrove plantation efforts in the Kori Creek and Sir Creek areas, visited the seaweed seed bank and interacted with experts, and met seaweed cultivators and beneficiaries of the MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) programme.
Planted Avicennia marina, a species of Mangrove, in the Jakhau Mangrove Nursery in Kutch, Gujarat. 

Under the MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) programme initiated by PM Shri @narendramodi ji, Kutch is undertaking large-scale mangrove restoration, scientific nursery development and livelihood initiatives. Against a cumulative plantation target of 29,250 hectares for 2023–24 to 2026–27, mangrove plantation has been completed over 27,652 hectares, including 12,450 hectares in the Kori Creek area. 

Approximately 3.49 lakh mangrove seedlings have been raised at the Jakhau Mangrove Nursery.

Interacted with subject experts to understand the challenges and technological and nature-based solutions to address the same.

Kutch is developing a comprehensive model of mangrove conservation by combining large-scale plantation, nurseries, biodiversity conservation, innovative tidal technology, renewable energy, community participation and sustainable livelihoods. 

Jakhau Mangrove Nursery is a significant example of technology-driven and community-oriented mangrove restoration in Gujarat.

title: DRI seizes more than 362 MT Pakistan-origin dry dates under ‘Operation Deep Manifest’
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 12:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant crackdown on attempts to circumvent India’s prohibition on imports from Pakistan, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has seized more than 362 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin dry dates.
Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted 13 containers of dry dates imported by a Mumbai-based firm at CFS Ambad, Nashik. The consignments had arrived from Jebel Ali, UAE, with import documents declaring the UAE as the country of origin.
Preliminary investigation revealed a carefully orchestrated transshipment arrangement designed to conceal the Pakistan-origin of the goods. The dry dates were initially shipped from Karachi Port, Pakistan, to Jebel Ali Port, UAE, in one set of containers aboard one vessel. At Jebel Ali, the goods were merely transshipped and trans
ferred to another set of containers and loaded onto a different vessel for onward shipment to India through entities operated by Pakistani nationals.
Following the Pahalgam terror attack, the Government of India, in the interest of national security, imposed a complete prohibition on the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, with effect from 2 May 2025, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 2 May 2025. In response, DRI, under “Operation Deep Manifest”, has been consistently identifying, intercepting and seizing Pakistan-origin goods attempted to be imported into India through third-country routing.
The seizure underscores DRI’s sustained resolve to identify, disrupt and dismantle sophisticated networks seeking to circumvent trade prohibitions through misdeclaration, transshipment and manipulation of documentation, thereby safeguarding national security and straightening supply chain integrity.

date:

                14 SEP 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed Hindi Diwas 2026 and the 6th All India Official Language Conference in Mumbai as the Chief Guest. On the occasion, Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Eknath Shinde and Smt. Sunetra Pawar, Union Ministers of State for Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai and Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar and Secretary, Department of Official Language, Smt. Anshuli Arya among several other dignitaries were present.
Extending greetings on Hindi Diwas and Ganesh Chaturthi, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that it is a “Manikanchan Yog” a rare and auspicious coincidence, that Hindi Diwas and Ganesh Chaturthi are being celebrated on the same day. He said that Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles would pave the way for the development of Indian languages and remove the obstacles along that path. Recalling Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak on the occasion, Shri Shah said that the public celebration of Ganesh Utsav in Maharashtra was started by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak Maharaj in 1893. He said that Tilak Maharaj had correctly understood the pulse of the country. He deeply understood that awareness and cultural nationalism in India could be generated only through its culture and history. Therefore, he initiated the celebration of Ganesh Utsav and the birth anniversary of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He said that before long, both these festivals began to be celebrated across the country. These two festivals caused considerable concern for the British. Through these festivals, Tilak Maharaj generated a tremendous wave of patriotism among the people. Shri Shah said that Maharashtra is a land of traditions and expansive thinking. He said that during the Bhakti movement, several saints from Maharashtra composed works that gave considerable impetus to the Bhakti movement across the country. He said that Maharashtra is the land of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, who made "Swaraj, Swadharma and Swabhasha" —self-rule, one's own faith and one's own language, fundamental elements of Swaraj. By giving Marathi prominence in administration he created a rich repository of terminology in his own language. This system continued to serve as the basis of governance during the era of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Hindavi Swaraj.
Shri Amit Shah said that today the training programmes in Hindi word processing, Hindi typing and shorthand were inaugurated. Shri Shah also presented the Rajbhasha Kirti Awards and Rajbhasha Gaurav Awards. He congratulated all the recipients of these honours. Shri Shah said that today, publications such as ‘Shiv Anadi Hain, Anant Hain’, ‘Bharatiya Gyan Tantra: Srot Aur Swaroop’, ‘Andheron Se Ujalon Tak’, a special commemorative edition of the Department of Official Language’s journal ‘Rajbhasha Bharati’ centred on the National Song ‘Vande Mataram’, and ‘150 Chapters of Vande Mataram’ were released.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that “Vande Mataram” is not an ordinary song. It was Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's great effort to awaken Indian consciousness during a period of intense colonial subjugation. Through his poetry, he sought to shake the sleeping consciousness of India. His song "Vande Mataram" written in "Anandamath", soon became a declaration of freedom throughout India. Through the call of "Vande Mataram", Bankim Chandra not only awakened a deep yearning and intense desire for freedom but also laid the foundation of India's cultural nationalism. Shri Shah said that unfortunately, "Vande Mataram" was later divided into parts. Even after Independence, it took Parliament nearly 80 years to accept it in its complete form. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is the leader who took the initiative to have "Vande Mataram" sung again at official functions in its complete form and with its full glory.
Shri Amit Shah said that the Hindi Diwas programme being held on the land of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj during the 150th year of Vande Mataram would take forward the journey of the Official Language and Indian languages in the coming days. Paying tribute to Maharashtra's multilingual culture, Shri Shah said that Marathi is respected here and it should be. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi was the first to grant Marathi the status of a Classical Language. Konkani, Gujarati, Sindhi, Hindi, Kannada, Warli and several other languages have also developed in Maharashtra and received respect and recognition. He said that Maharashtra is the most multilingual state in the entire country. He also congratulated the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Ministers of Maharashtra for establishing an inclusive system in the state administration that accepts everyone.
Quoting Acharya Vinoba Bhave, Union Home Minister and Cooperation Minister said, “If I had not taken the support of Hindi, I would not have been able to take the revolutionary message of Bhoodan and Gramdan to the people in every village of Kashmir, Assam and Kerala. If I had relied on another language, I would not have been able to work in the villages at all. It was the Official Language that taught me how to communicate with every village.” Home Minister said that the Official Language has this connection with all the languages of the country because all these languages have been part of India's everyday speech for centuries and have been in mutual interaction for hundreds of years. He said that he himself comes from Gujarat, where Gujarati not Hindi is spoken. However, when he was given the responsibility of working at the national level, he faced no difficulty in working across the country because he understands and speaks Hindi. He said that the Official Language gave him a tremendous opportunity to work across the country.
Shri Amit Shah said that Maharashtra is the land of Veer Savarkar. Savarkar was one of the most learned linguists of his time. He coined many words that did not previously exist in Indian languages. All these words were readily accepted in Marathi, the Official Language and other Indian languages. He also worked to purify the Marathi language by assimilating the ideas expressed in Tilak's writings. Shri Shah said that the Department of Official Language has honoured Veer Savarkar by accepting all the words that he revised and coined in the online dictionary “Hindi Shabd-Sindhu.” He said that the makers of the Constitution deliberately and thoughtfully decided on 14 September 1949 to adopt Hindi as the Official Language. Shri Shah said that since Shri Narendra Modi became Prime Minister, the Department of Official Language has achieved numerous milestones. He said that one of the biggest initiatives was undertaken through the National Education Policy. Prime Minister Modi has made learning one's mother tongue in primary education mandatory. No child can grow into a complete individual without learning his or her mother tongue because the affection of a mother and the love of a sister or brother cannot be fully understood without one's mother tongue. Attachment to one's land, language, faith, traditions, culture and values is possible through the mother tongue. Therefore, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has made the mother tongue mandatory in primary education. Shri Amit Shah said that a child can progress only after learning his or her mother tongue. The process of thinking begins in the mother tongue. When a person thinks, analyses and makes decisions, doing so in the mother tongue leads to better thinking, better analysis and better decisions. Shri Shah said that, alongside this, Prime Minister Modi has also made learning another Indian language mandatory. He said that those who oppose the learning of Indian languages do not realise how serious a mistake they are making. Children should learn Indian languages. Learning a second Indian language means that a child will automatically become connected with the goal of “Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat”. Along with learning their mother tongue, if children learn another Indian language, they will automatically connect with their Indian identity and, freed from narrow-minded thinking, become true citizens committed to India. He said that the government wants to enrich every language of India.
Union Home Minister said that in 2019, it was decided that the All India Official Language Conference would not remain confined to Delhi but would be organised in different states across the country on a rotational basis. Since then, today's event marks the sixth conference. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi Ji, four volumes of the Official Language Committee’s reports have been submitted to the Hon’ble President since 2019. A total of 13 volumes have been completed so far, four of them during Modi's tenure. He said that whenever Prime Minister Modi has travelled to a major global platform or another country and delivered a speech, he has spoken in the Official Language and Indian languages. Hearing the country's Prime Minister speak in his own language instead of a foreign language at major global forums fills every Indian with pride. Prime Minister Modi has also facilitated the teaching of the Official Language at universities in several countries. More than 5 lakh employees of the Government of India have been trained. The AI-based “Kanthasth 2.0” platform has been opened to foreigners as well, with more than 50 million sentences.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that LILA Rajbhasha and LILA Pravah (LILA – Learn Indian Languages through Artificial Intelligence) have produced very good results. The “Hindi Shabd-Sindhu” dictionary, which began with 51,000 words, has now grown to 800,000 words. He said that more than 50,000 words from local languages have been incorporated into "Hindi Shabd-Sindhu", making Hindi more flexible and adaptable. He expressed confidence that by 2029, this dictionary would become the world's largest dictionary. He said that wherever there were gaps in Hindi and no word existed for a particular concept, more than 50,000 words from local languages were adopted to make the Official Language more flexible. These include Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, Odia and other languages. More than 50,000 words from each language have been incorporated into "Hindi Shabd-Sindhu". He said that the Department of Official Language has developed “Bharti – Bahubhashi Anuvad Sarathi” and has also launched the “Indian Languages Section.”
Union Home Minister said that the government wants to make Indian languages languages of governance and science, enrich literature, and connect Indian languages with one another to create a vast collective linguistic resource. Whether it is the JEE, NEET or an undergraduate entrance examination, these examinations are now conducted in 13 languages.
Shri Amit Shah said that he would like to tell those who try to create disputes between languages that a child can truly understand India only through his or her mother tongue. If the child attempts to understand India through a foreign language, there is a possibility of misunderstanding it. Therefore, he urged everyone to set aside political differences and focus on promoting Indian languages. He said that among the “Panch Pran” given by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to the people of the country from the ramparts of the Red Fort is the pledge to free India from the mindset of slavery.
Union Home Minister said that, when it comes to languages, there can be no greater personality than Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore. He had said, “Indian culture and Indian literature are like a fully developed hundred-petalled lotus, each petal representing our regional languages. The destruction of even one petal would destroy the beauty of the lotus. Let the regional languages remain as queens in their respective provinces, while Hindi, as the central jewel among all these languages, continues to enhance the beauty of this hundred-petalled lotus.” Shri Amit Shah said that poet Rabindranath Tagore had made this observation after deep thought.  He said that India's languages may certainly be different notes, but the song is one, the song of patriotism is one and the song of our culture is one. There is no objection to having many languages. The sentiment must remain Indian. There may be many dialects, but India's voice must remain one.

title: Message of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah on Hindi Diwas 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 12:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Dear fellow citizens,
Warm greetings to all of you on the occasion of Hindi Diwas!
Our country is a unique land of linguistic diversity and rich cultural heritage. Many people say that the fact that we have different languages is a weakness, but I believe that having so many languages is our greatest strength. Every language carries with it a history, folk traditions and a distinct worldview, which also help carry forward the values and cultural ethos of our younger generations. This linguistic plurality strengthens the spirit of
‘Unity in Diversity’
that defines India. Language is not merely a means of communication; it is the memory of a society and its sense of self.
Amid this diversity, Hindi has played an important role as a language of dialogue, communication and coordination, bringing together people from different sections and communities across the country. The development of Hindi can truly be meaningful only when it progresses alongside the respect, preservation and promotion of all Indian languages. Hindi is not a competitor to any language; rather, it is an important link for fostering a sense of affinity and dialogue among Indian languages and strengthening national unity. The most beautiful testimony to this truth lies in our own history.
Swami Dayanand Saraswati Ji
was a native Gujarati speaker, yet he wrote
Satyarth Prakash
in Hindi.
Mahatma Gandhi
established the
Dakshina Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha
in Madras in 1918.
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
was a Bengali speaker, yet he adopted Hindi as the language of communication of the
Azad Hind Fauj
and gave the nation the inspiring slogan
‘Jai Hind’
. Thus, people from diverse linguistic backgrounds have made the greatest contribution towards making Hindi a language of communication among the people. The immense contribution of these great personalities, whose mother tongue was never Hindi, remains a source of inspiration for all of us.
My own mother tongue is also Gujarati, but whenever I travel to any part of the country, the language that directly connects me with the common people there is Hindi. If we look at the journey of Hindi, we can see reflected in it the journey of the entire nation. From the
Padavali
of Vidyapati in the Adikal period and the heroic ballads of
Prithviraj Raso
, to the remarkable era of the Bhakti period—when Tulsidas Ji took the story of Lord Rama to every household and Surdas Ji gave a voice to the tender expression of parental affection.
During the freedom movement, the ideals of
Swaraj
,
Swadeshi
and
Swabhasha
infused new energy into the national consciousness. Our freedom fighters, too, had realised that the vision of
Swaraj
would remain incomplete without pride in our own language and identity. After Independence, Indian languages became the means of nation-building, governance and taking the development to every citizen. Hindi, along with all other Indian languages, played an important role in spreading the message of social awakening, national unity and the idea of freedom to every section of society. Carrying forward this rich legacy, the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi as the Official Language of the Union of India on
14 September 1949
.
However, a paradox also emerged after Independence. While we attained political freedom, the values of our own language, our own culture and our self-respect were pushed to the margins.
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, from the Red Fort, called upon the nation to free itself from this mindset of colonialism, and language has a pivotal role to play in this. The transformation of
Rajpath
into
Kartavya Path
was not merely a change of name. Replacing the colonial, punishment-oriented laws enacted by the British with three people-centric laws—the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam
—was not merely a change in terminology. It represents the restoration of our national self-pride.
Today, the
National Education Policy
places the mother tongue at the centre of education. Engineering and medical education is being imparted in Indian languages, and competitive examinations are being conducted in multiple Indian languages.
On the occasion of the
80th Independence Day
, the Prime Minister, from the Red Fort, called for
‘Saptadhara of Shakti’
—the seven streams of strength—for building a
Viksit Bharat
. The seventh stream is
India’s soft power
.
The greatest carrier of any nation’s soft power is its language. Yoga, Ayurveda, literature, cinema and our cultural strength—all reach the world through our languages.
There was once a concern that in the age of technology, Indian languages might be left behind. However, under the Modi Government, Hindi, along with all other Indian languages, is witnessing a
golden era of technological advancement
.
The
‘
Bharati’ tool
, an Artificial Intelligence-based tool developed by the Department of Official Language, is making communication among Indian languages more seamless today. The
‘
Hindi Shabd Sindhu’
, a digital dictionary with more than
8.27 lakh entries
, has emerged as a rich platform for knowledge sharing. The
‘Indian Language Section’
, established in 2024, is facilitating administrative communication in Indian languages. AI and translation technologies have brought down the barriers of language. Today, every Indian can think in their own language and communicate with the entire world. At the same time, during the tenure of the Modi Government, the
Parliamentary Committee on Official Language
has submitted four new volumes of its reports to the Hon’ble President.
At the end, I would like to say something to the youth. Learn as many languages of the world as you can, but never abandon your own language. I would also urge all parents across the country to make it a point to communicate with your children in their mother tongue. There can be no greater inferiority complex than the thought,
“If I speak in my own language, I will be considered inferior.”
Language is what connects us with our mother, our soil, our history and our culture. This year also marks the
150th anniversary of the composition of the national song, ‘Vande Mataram’
—a song that transformed language into a weapon of freedom.
Let us, on this occasion, resolve to make
Hindi and all Indian languages
powerful instruments in our journey towards building a
Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Once again, my heartfelt greetings to all of you on
Official Language Day
.
Vande Mataram!

title: Kerala’s EcoSense Scholarships: Empowering 46000 Students to Champion Waste Management
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
From classrooms to communities, Kerala’s EcoSense initiative is turning students into active champions of waste management under Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0. With nearly 46,000 scholarships awarded, the programme is building green skills and fostering sustainable habits among young citizens.
What if the journey towards a Garbage Free City could begin not at a waste processing facility, but inside a classroom? Kerala is doing exactly that.
Across India, the Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0 (SBM-U 2.0) is driving a new generation of initiatives that go beyond infrastructure and waste management systems to focus on people, participation and behavioural change. By engaging children and youth in practical waste-management activities, these programmes are helping make segregation, reuse, resource conservation and sustainable living a part of everyday life.
Kerala’s Student Green Brigade Scholarship – EcoSense is a powerful example of this approach. Led by the Local Self Government Department, in collaboration with the General Education Department, Kerala, the initiative is turning schools into spaces where young minds do not just learn about waste management—they actively practise it.
Implemented under the leadership of the Local Self Government Department, in collaboration with the General Education Department, Government of Kerala, EcoSense has emerged as one of the State’s largest student-focused initiatives on waste management. The programme aims to provide scholarships to 50,000 students for their active engagement in waste management while nurturing a generation equipped with green skills and a strong sense of environmental responsibility.
The scholarship programme goes beyond creating awareness. It seeks to promote scientific waste management practices, encourage students to develop innovative solutions to local waste-related challenges, reduce waste generation and build practical understanding of sustainable waste management systems.
Under the scheme, 50 students from each Grama Panchayat, 75 students from each Municipality and 100 students from each Corporation are selected for the scholarship. This year, students from Classes 6 and 7 in the Upper Primary category, Classes 8 and 9 in the High School category, and first-year students of Higher Secondary and Vocational Higher Secondary categories were included.
Each selected student receives a scholarship of ₹1,500 along with a certificate of recognition, providing both encouragement and acknowledgement of their contribution towards Swachhata.
The scale of participation reflects the growing interest among Kerala’s students in environmental action. This year, the scholarship is being distributed to 45,880 students across 986 Local Self Government Institutions. Around five lakh students from nearly 9,000 schools participated in the programme, turning the initiative into a State-wide movement of learning and action.
The programme was designed to give students hands-on exposure to waste management practices rather than limiting their engagement to classroom discussions. Through a range of activities, students explored waste management systems within their own homes, ways to reduce waste generation, adherence to the Green Protocol, and the principles of Green School and Clean School initiatives. They also gained practical knowledge of composting and the reuse of discarded materials.
At the school level, students and teachers took up diverse activities that translated these concepts into action. These included setting up bins for source-level waste segregation, developing systems to convert biodegradable waste into compost, establishing repair shops and promoting organic farming. Students also participated in household visits, swap shops and cleanliness clubs, while creatively reusing discarded materials through craft activities.
A particularly important aspect of the programme was the exposure provided through visits to Material Collection Facilities (MCFs) and Resource Recovery Facilities (RRFs). Such visits helped students understand what happens to waste after it leaves their homes and highlighted the importance of segregation at source for effective resource recovery and scientific waste management.
Students were also encouraged to take an active role in identifying and addressing waste-management concerns in their communities. Activities included reporting violations related to waste management and undertaking student-led household visits, enabling young participants to become ambassadors of responsible waste practices among their families and neighbourhoods.
Throughout November, Green Assemblies (Haritha Sabhas) were organised for children in schools across Kerala, creating another avenue for students to discuss environmental issues, share ideas and collectively explore solutions for better waste management.
By placing students at the heart of waste-management action, EcoSense demonstrates how youth can become powerful partners in building sustainable communities. From segregating waste at home and composting biodegradable waste to reusing discarded materials and understanding resource recovery, students are not merely learning about Swachhata—they are practising it.

title: From Coconut Husk to Enterprise: How Coir is transforming Rural lives
subtitle: Coir Emerges as a Catalyst for Rural Entrepreneurship, Women's Empowerment and Sustainable Livelihoods
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 2:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
What begins as coconut husk is becoming a source of enterprise and livelihood across India’s coconut-growing regions. Coir, a natural, durable and eco-friendly fibre, has been part of India’s rural economy for generations. Today, entrepreneurs are increasingly converting it into value-added products ranging from mats and ropes to handicrafts, bio-fertilisers and innovative packaging solutions. Behind this transformation are thousands of rural entrepreneurs and artisans who are turning a traditional activity into modern livelihoods. With support from the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), particularly through the Coir Board and the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), coir is becoming a pathway to self-employment, women’s empowerment and local economic growth.
Turning Coir Waste into a Thriving Enterprise:
One Enterprise, 120 Women, Countless Opportunities
In Kadiyam, East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh,
Ms. Allam Gowthamy
transformed coconut fibre and coir waste into a successful enterprise. She received specialised training at the Coir Board Training Centre, Dhawaleswaram and established
Adigo Coir Products
in 2024–25
with a project cost of ₹10 lakh
, supported by a ₹6.50 lakh bank loan and PMEGP assistance. The unit now produces eco-friendly doormats, ropes, decorative dolls and handicrafts.
The enterprise has achieved an
annual turnover of around ₹35 lakh and a profit of approximately ₹10 lakh,
while generating direct employment for six women. But her impact extends beyond her own enterprise. She has trained nearly 120 women in coir mat weaving, rope making and handicraft production, helping them develop livelihood opportunities. Her success has also inspired around 5 additional coir units in nearby areas with Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme.
2.
Shri Surendran’s Green Coir Success Story
Turning coir pith into an opportunity for sustainable agriculture,
Shri P. Surendran
established
Sampoorna Plus Agro Fertilizer Enterprises (SAFE)
in Kozhikode, Kerala, in November 2024. With training and technical support from the Coir Board, Kannur and Central Coir Research Institute (CCRI), Kalavoor, he began producing eco-friendly coir pith bio-fertilizer that improves soil fertility and moisture retention.
In just one year his enterprise has built a customer base of 500+, sold over 20 tonnes of bio-fertilizer and generated a turnover of ₹13 lakh, with a profit of ₹4 lakh in FY 2024–25. The unit also employs five workers, including two women, creating local livelihood opportunities. From coir waste to a sustainable business, his journey shows how innovation and technical support can create new business opportunities from materials that might otherwise have limited economic value.
Why Coir Matters to Rural India
Coir is one of India’s oldest natural fibres. Organised coir production in India began in 1859 with the establishment of the first coir factory in Alappuzha, Kerala
.
Since then, the sector has grown across major coconut-producing regions. India is the world’s largest producer of coir and accounts for more than 80 per cent of global coir fibre production
.
The industry is also closely linked with women’s livelihoods. Women account for nearly 80 per cent of those engaged in fibre extraction and spinning
.
This makes coir an important rural livelihood sector—connecting coconut farmers, workers, women artisans, cooperatives, entrepreneurs, manufacturers and exporters.
From Fibre to Finished Product
The potential of coir extends well beyond the production of raw fibre. Through processing, design and innovation, coir can be transformed into a wide range of higher-value products, including:
Mats and doormats
Ropes and yarn
Brushes and other household products
Decorative items and handicrafts
Garden and horticulture products
Innovative and eco-friendly packaging solutions
Supporting the Coir Value Chain
The
Coir Board
, a statutory body under the Ministry of MSME, works to strengthen the sector through skill development, technology, research, market promotion, exports and welfare initiatives.
The Coir Vikas Yojana (CVY) supports areas such as technology and research, skill development, women’s training, domestic and international market promotion, industry development and worker welfare. The objective is to enable people associated with the coir sector to acquire new skills, adopt better technology, produce quality products and access larger markets. At the same time, exhibitions, fairs, showrooms and export promotion activities are helping coir producers showcase their products and connect with new customers and markets.
Innovation: Giving Coir a New Identity
The Central Coir Research Institute has developed
eco-friendly coir rail wheel axle packaging
cups as an alternative to HDPE plastic cups. Such innovations show how a traditional natural fibre can find applications in modern industries while supporting environmentally responsible production.
A Fibre with a Bigger Purpose
The stories of Shri Allam Gowthamy and Shri G. Sabu illustrate the changing face of India’s coir sector. With skills, finance, technology, research and market support, India’s traditional coir sector is steadily moving towards higher-value products and modern enterprises—turning locally available resources into opportunities for entrepreneurship and prosperity.
For more information, visit at:
https://coirboard.gov.in/

Dr Jitendra Singh Says India Post’s Expanding Service Network Can Further Strengthen Government-Citizen Connect

content:
Representatives of All India employee organisations of the Department of Posts hailed the Government for 'reinventing' India Post and thanked PM Sh
ri
Narendra Modi for turning it into a modern, citizen-centric service network, saying that the changes have significantly expanded the role of India Post and brought a wide range of citizen-centric services closer to people across the country. They said that India Post today goes far beyond traditional mail delivery, with faster delivery services, Aadhaar-related facilities, PAN and Passport Seva services, doorstep banking and digital pension services strengthening its public-service role.
A delegation of representatives of All India employee organisations of the Department of Posts called on Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh, at Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi, today. The delegation discussed the transformation of postal services as well as various matters concerning employees, employee organisations and pensioners.
During the interaction, the representatives spoke about the expansion of India Post’s service portfolio over the past decade, including delivery within 24 hours in applicable services, Aadhaar-related services and the availability of PAN and Passport Seva facilities through the postal network. They also spoke about the growing role of India Post in providing banking and financial services at the doorstep, particularly in rural areas.
Dr Jitendra Singh said that the transformation of India Post is reflected in the changing role of the postman, who today is increasingly taking banking and other essential services directly to citizens. From traditional letter delivery, the postal network has expanded into a wider platform for delivering financial and citizen services, with its extensive reach providing an important last-mile connection between government services and people.
The Minister said that the expansion of India Post Payments Bank and doorstep banking has enabled the postal network to take financial services to villages and households, allowing citizens to access banking facilities closer to their homes. The postal network has also expanded services such as Digital Life Certificates for pensioners, making essential pension-related services more accessible and convenient.
Dr Jitendra Singh also recalled the important role played by postal employees during the COVID-19 pandemic, when the postal network continued to provide essential services despite the nationwide lockdown. Postal personnel helped take banking services and cash to citizens at their homes, while postal vehicles and infrastructure were also utilised for the delivery and movement of essential medical and protective supplies.
The Minister said that the vast nationwide network of the Department of Posts is a valuable public-service asset and can be utilised more extensively for government programmes, citizen outreach and last-mile delivery. The delegation also expressed its willingness to contribute to efforts aimed at making greater use of the postal network for public-service delivery and government initiatives.
During the interaction, the delegation placed before Dr Jitendra Singh various service-related and organisational matters concerning postal employees, including issues relating to verification and recognition of employee organisations, representation in departmental forums, pensioners and certain long-pending service matters.
The delegation also raised matters concerning certain categories of employees and service benefits. Dr Jitendra Singh said that matters requiring examination would be considered through the appropriate administrative process, keeping in view the applicable rules as well as legal and financial implications.
The interaction also covered the need to further strengthen the delivery of citizen-centric services through the postal network and to make effective use of its vast nationwide reach in support of government initiatives.
The delegation thanked Dr Jitendra Singh for the interaction and for giving representatives an opportunity to place their service-related matters before the Government.

title: NHAI to Transform 1033 National Highway Helpline with New Technology
subtitle: New system to help National Highway users get faster assistance during emergencies, vehicle breakdowns and other highway-related problems
date:

                14 SEP 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
National Highways Authority of India (
NHAI
)
is planning to upgrade its existing 1033 National Highway Helpline with advanced technology to provide faster and better assistance to people travelling on National Highways. The upgraded 1033 helpline will use technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), real-time location tracking and smart emergency-response systems. These improvements will help the 1033 National Highway helpline identify the location of callers, understand calls in different Indian languages and send the right assistance to the location more quickly. Human operators will continue to play an important role, especially in emergencies where human judgement and decision-making are essential.
1033 Helpline provides round-the-clock assistance
The 1033 helpline was introduced in 2018 and is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. It helps National Highway users with:
Medical emergencies.
Vehicle breakdowns.
Assistance from ambulances, cranes and patrol vehicles.
Toll plaza and FASTag-related issues.
Other problems faced while travelling on National Highways.
The helpline currently covers more than 1.46 lakh km of National Highways and receives around 15,000 calls every day. It also provides assistance in multiple languages.
What will improve with the new system?
The Next Generation 1033 platform is aimed at providing the following benefits:
Faster assistance: Better systems for receiving calls and sending help to the required location.
Location identification: Real-time capture of the caller’s location to help emergency teams reach the spot.
Multilingual support: AI-assisted handling of calls in different Indian languages.
Smart dispatch: Intelligent systems to help identify and send the most suitable ambulance, crane or patrol vehicle.
Proactive alerts: Timely advisories to highway users about incidents and other important developments.
Better coordination: Improved coordination between the helpline, emergency services and National Highway operations teams.
Indian Highways Management Company Limited (IHMCL), a company promoted by NHAI, has invited an Expression of Interest (EOI) from companies and consortia for the development, design, deployment, operation and maintenance of the Next Generation 1033 Helpline and Call Centre.  The initiative requires expertise in software development, digital platforms, 24x7 call-centre operations and emergency-response services.  Companies working in mobility and ride-hailing, logistics, quick-commerce, public safety, Computer-Aided Dispatch, Voice AI and Indian-language speech-recognition technologies are encouraged to participate.
Industry feedback to help develop the new platform
IHMCL will seek suggestions and technical inputs from industry experts to develop a reliable, scalable and future-ready system. Relevant industry best practices will also be considered while finalising the requirements.
The upgraded 1033 helpline is expected to make assistance on National Highways faster, more coordinated and more convenient for citizens. By combining technology with human support, NHAI aims to further improve the safety and travel experience of highway users across the country.

title: Unusual wave-like heat transport in crystalline solid signals breakthrough converting waste heat in industries
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                14 SEP 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi
content:
An unusual heat transport regime detected in a newly studied copper chalcogenide material called thallium copper selenide (TlCu5Se3) could pave way for efficient conversion of waste heat to electricity via thermoelectric energy conversion in power plants, cement industries, steel plants, automobiles, data centres and battery heat management systems.
Conventional superionic materials can achieve low lattice thermal conductivity via highly mobile ions. But excessive ion migration may cause structural instability and compromise its thermoelectric performance. Confined ion diffusion, where ionic motion remains restricted within a complex crystalline framework, offers a way to suppress heat transport while preserving structural stability and promoting unconventional heat-transport mechanisms.
In crystalline materials, heat is conventionally understood to be transported by particle-like phonons, with phonon mean free path (MFP) typically much larger than the interatomic distance. In contrast, strong disorder and anharmonicity (phenomenon in which atomic vibrations become asymmetric and deviate significantly from normal parabolic behaviour, disrupting propagation of heat) in glasses reduce the MFP to nearly the interatomic length scale, suppressing conventional phonon propagation.
This conventional picture, however, becomes increasingly inadequate when strong anharmonicity and structural disorder can retain long-range crystallographic order while exhibiting highly localized, closely spaced vibrational modes that interact strongly with one another.
In this intermediate regime, thermal energy can be transported not only through particle-like phonon propagation but also through wave-like coherence between different vibrational modes, enabling ultralow lattice thermal conductivity. Such ultralow thermal conducting materials have immense importance in thermal barrier coatings, thermoelectric energy conversion, thermal decoherence free quantum technology.
Researchers at Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), Bengaluru (an autonomous institution under the Department of Science & Technology, Govt. of India) and other research team members have found an unusual wave-like thermal transport regime in a newly studied copper chalcogenide material, TlCu5Se3 that can lead to high-performance thermoelectric conversion.
The complex crystal framework of TlCu5Se3 was expected to restrict the motion of Cu atoms rather than allowing long-range migration providing opportunity to investigate whether this confined dynamic behaviour could generate strong anharmonicity and suppress heat transport without causing structural instability.
In this work, led by Prof. Kanishka Biswas and his Ph.D. students, Ms. Sayantoni Choudhury and Dr. Animesh Bhui from the New Chemistry Unit (NCU) at JNCASR, published in the prestigious journal, Science Advances, investigated the structural and thermoelectric properties through experiments and conducted advanced theoretical calculations to understand the origin of the unusual heat transport.
They showed that the complex crystal structure and intrinsically confined dynamic disorder of the Cu sublattice generate exceptionally strong anharmonicity, leading to predominantly wave-like phonon transport and an intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
Fig 1: A schematic illustrating the complex knot-like structural framework that leads to a confined Cu dynamic, resulting in unusual heat transport and ultrahigh thermoelectric performance in TlCu5Se3.
This unusual thermal transport, together with favorable electronic transport, give rise to one of the highest thermoelectric performances (thermoelectric figure of merit, zT of 1.7) among pristine ternary chalcogenides. The origin of this unusual behaviour lies in the distinctive crystal framework of TlCu5Se3. The compound crystallizes in a tetragonal structure and forms a complex three-dimensional cloverleaf knot-like framework with open channels along the crystallographic c-axis.
The intrinsic bonding hierarchy associated with this complex framework leads to these confined dynamics. To probe the presence of this confined dynamic behaviour of Cu, the team collaborated with Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare and his postdoc Dr. Prasad V. Matukumilli from the Theoretical Sciences Unit (TSU), JNCASR, Bengaluru, to perform advanced first-principles theoretical calculations and molecular-dynamics simulations.
Fig 2: Prof. Kanishka Biswas (left) and Sayantoni Choudhury (right) JNCASR, Bangalore.
Molecular-dynamics simulations (computer simulations of atomic motions over time) reveal that Cu atoms exhibit localized dynamic disorder rather than the long-range, liquid-like diffusion characteristic of superionic copper chalcogenides. This confined motion acts primarily as a source of strong lattice anharmonicity. As a direct consequence, heat begins to propagate through wave-like coherence, with phonons tunnelling between localized vibrational states rather than moving as well-defined particles. To uncover how these unusual vibrations transport heat, the researchers went beyond the conventional phonon-gas model and employed the unified formalism of thermal transport. This framework considers both particle-like phonon propagation and wave-like coherence between different phonon branches.
The significance of this work extends beyond thermoelectric performance, which establishes how structural complexity and confined ion dynamics can lead to an unconventional mechanism for thermal management and high-performance thermoelectric energy conversion.

content:
The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) enables aspiring scholars to pursue doctoral education by addressing financial barriers.
Smt. Midhila Radhakrishnan’s journey reflects how this fellowship support has helped her secure admission, focus on research and strengthen her capabilities as an educator and researcher.
Smt. Midhila Radhakrishnan, a 30-year-old scholar from Thrissur district, Kerala, is pursuing her Ph.D. with support under NFSC.
Currently in the fourth year of her doctoral programme, she has published four research papers in Scopus-indexed journals—two in Q1 and two in Q2 categories.
Her aspiration to pursue research grew while working as an Assistant Professor in a college. As she guided students, she recognised the need to deepen her research knowledge to address their questions and support their projects more effectively. This experience motivated her to pursue doctoral studies.
However, translating this aspiration into reality required financial support. As a fresher, her college salary was low and insufficient to support her doctoral ambitions independently. Although her family was financially stable, she had chosen not to depend on them for her expenses after completing post-graduation.
Her university required Ph.D. applicants to hold a fellowship, making financial assistance essential for admission. The award of the NFSC fellowship in 2020 opened a path forward. Midhila joined her Ph.D. programme in 2022, and fellowship assistance began in June that year.
Through fellowship, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency assistance, NFSC has helped her manage the expenses associated with doctoral study. She reports receiving ₹42,000 as Senior Research Fellowship support and ₹8,400 as HRA. Consistent financial assistance has enabled her to concentrate on research without economic stress and provide compensation to participants involved in her research work.
Her four publications in Scopus-indexed journals mark significant progress in her ongoing doctoral journey. The fellowship has remained a source of motivation, supporting her efforts to develop the research expertise that first inspired her to pursue a Ph.D.
Talking about the help and support,
Smt. Midhila Radhakrishnan said,
“NFSC support enabled me to pursue my PhD and focus on research without financial stress.”
Midhila Radhakrishnan’s journey illustrates how NFSC support enables aspiring researchers to overcome financial and admission barriers, pursue doctoral education and strengthen their contribution to teaching and academia.

Counselling and rehabilitation assistance supported his personal development and helped him acquire skills needed to rebuild his life. Community support and preventive interventions strengthened his recovery and supported social reintegration and long-term rehabilitation.
The treatment, counselling, empathy and community support helped Mrinas rebuild his life and move towards greater stability.
Today, Mrinas is a full-time employee. His aspiration to serve in the IRBN remains part of his hopes for the future. DBT, Aadhaar-Based Authentication, Digital Verification Strengthen Transparency And Scholarship Delivery
date:

                14 SEP 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, has undertaken targeted interventions to strengthen equitable access to education for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).
Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment Shri Sudhansh Pant said that the Department is supporting educational continuity and reducing financial barriers for socially and educationally disadvantaged communities, through scholarships, residential infrastructure, overseas education assistance, fellowships, coaching initiatives and digital reforms.
Shri Pant said these interventions seek to improve access to quality institutions and support students across different stages of education. He added that specific emphasis has been placed on transparent scholarship delivery, beneficiary authentication and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)-enabled systems.
The Secretary informed that the Pre-Matric Scholarships Scheme for Scheduled Castes and Others is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at promoting literacy, reducing dropout rates and ensuring continuity of education at the pre-matric level. It supports children belonging to Scheduled Castes and children of parents or guardians engaged in unclean and hazardous occupations. He said through targeted financial assistance, the scheme strengthens educational inclusion and helps students from disadvantaged backgrounds continue their school education.
Shri Pant informed that during FY 2014–15 to FY 2025–26, Central Assistance amounting to Rs 4,893.03 Crore was released under the scheme, with reported annual beneficiary figures totalling approximately 299.66 lakh over the period. During FY 2025–26 alone, Rs 562.36 Crore was released, benefiting 26.79 lakh students, he added.
Stating that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste students is a flagship Centrally Sponsored intervention, the Secretary said that Scheme is designed to improve access to higher education among students from economically disadvantaged SC households. He added that the Scheme seeks to reduce financial barriers in post-secondary education, strengthen retention and enhance the Gross Enrolment Ratio of SC students in higher education institutions.
The Secretary further informed that during FY 2014–15 to FY 2025–26, Central Assistance amounting to Rs 46,581.54 Crore was released under the scheme, with reported annual beneficiary figures totalling 612.98 lakh over the period. During FY 2025–26, Central Assistance of Rs 6,186.95 crore was released, benefiting 47.53 lakh students.
Digital Reforms Strengthen Transparency and Beneficiary Authentication
Describing digital reforms to strengthen transparency and authentication, Shri Pant said that from FY 2021–22 onwards, the Department transitioned the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme to a DBT-enabled framework, facilitating direct transfer of scholarship assistance into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries. He said this reform has strengthened accountability, reduced delays and leakages, and improved last-mile delivery.
The Secretary further stated that the Department has introduced de-duplication mechanisms to identify and eliminate fake and duplicate beneficiaries, alongside biometric authentication and e-KYC-based verification of beneficiaries and officials. Integration with DigiLocker and API SETU facilitates digital verification of certificates and documents, he added.
Shri Pant informed that One-Time Registration has been introduced to enable tracking of beneficiaries across schemes and academic years. He said integration with AISHE, UDISE, NCVT and SCVT databases supports validation of institutional and student records, while multi-layered checks help minimize discrepancies and duplication.
The Secretary said linkages with UIDAI, NPCI and PFMS further support seamless processing and direct disbursement of scholarship assistance which strengthen beneficiary authentication, improve fund-flow management and support a more transparent and accountable scholarship delivery system.
The Secretary expressed hope that through sustained financial assistance and technology-enabled reforms, the Department would continue to strengthen educational opportunities for disadvantaged communities, supporting students in continuing their education and accessing higher learning.
